text: Admin users + server-wide settings tab (registration toggle, reset password, delete user)
actually runtime configuration of the user-registration-feature shall not persist across restarts. after restart the server default shall apply again

DESIGN SETTLED (supersedes the persistence/CLI/is_admin parts of the body above):

1. Admin identity = STATIC CONFIG ONLY. A blueprint variable
   `create_blueprint(admin_emails=[...])`, stored per-instance like
   allow_registration. An account is admin iff `lower(g.account.email)` is in the
   lower()-normalized (and stripped) admin_emails set, checked live.
   REMOVED vs body: no `accounts.is_admin` column, no migration for admin, no
   grant/revoke CLI. Admin is unwritable at runtime by construction. Lower risk.

2. Registration override is EPHEMERAL (resets to config default on restart) AND
   this is deployed MULTI-WORKER, so it needs shared, non-durable state:
   - New small DB table (e.g. `server_runtime`) holding the override value + the
     BOOT ID it was written under.
   - boot id = the master process start-time (getppid + /proc/<ppid>/stat, or
     psutil create_time). All workers of one server run share it; it changes on
     restart. Read LAZILY at request time — so preload-vs-not / which-worker /
     when-registration-ran are all irrelevant (this is the answer to "you can't
     identify server startup from a blueprint": don't — compare staleness at read).
   - Register route honors the override only when stored boot id == current boot
     id; on a mismatch it DELETES the stale row (self-cleaning) and falls back to
     the config default.
   - Requires a migration for the table (the feature's only schema change).
   - The web auth page must read the EFFECTIVE flag from a runtime endpoint, not
     the baked `<meta name="app-allow-registration">` (which can't reflect a live
     toggle).

3. Step-up password confirmation (reuse `_require_password`) on the two
   account-affecting admin actions: delete user + reset password. NOT on the
   registration toggle (non-destructive, reversible).

4. Delete user: refuse to delete an account whose email is a config admin; no
   self-delete via the admin path (self-delete stays in personal settings).

5. Admin API behind `admin_required`: GET /admin/users, GET/PUT the registration
   override, POST reset-password (returns new password once, relayed out-of-band),
   DELETE user. Client learns admin status via login/settings response → renders
   the extra tab only when true. Web page + Android Compose screen.

Broader email case-sensitivity (normalize-at-write vs lower()-at-every-read) was
discussed and left as a SEPARATE potential ticket — the codebase is currently
consistent (login/reset/invite-redeem/unique-index all lower()), no live bug.

Implemented across all three components (commits e1e6c9b server, b5b5a36 web,
173dcd2 android, cdd49da docs) per the settled design.

Server: static admin_emails config + admin_required; server_runtime table
(migration 4) + boot-id-tagged registration override (resets on restart,
consistent across workers); admin API (users list, GET/PUT server-settings,
reset-password, delete user) with step-up on the admin's own password; login
response carries is_admin; public /registration-status. Migration 4 verified
end-to-end on a real v1.6.1 DB.

Web: AdminPage (/admin, reached from Settings when admin) — registration toggle,
users list with reset (shown once) / delete (step-up); LoginPage reads the live
registration flag.

Android: AdminScreen + AdminViewModel (Routes.ADMIN, entry from Settings);
is_admin stored in the session at login.

Verified: server 276 passed (15 new in test_admin.py); web 142 passed (AdminPage
tests); android :app:testDebugUnitTest + :app:lintDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL
(AdminViewModelTest). NOT released — batched on main for the next release.

Deferred/notes: is_admin lives only in the login response (not GET /settings), so
a config change granting admin needs a re-login to take effect — acceptable, since
admin_emails changes require a config edit + restart anyway. No is_admin column /
CLI, by design (config is the only source).
